title: Define scope and rules of engagement
assessment: Ownership/authorization asserted. This assessment is confined to supplied source and sandbox-only checks; no remote systems are tested.

title: Inventory entry points
assessment: Literal routes inventoried, but dynamic CRUD factories, enabled plugins and stored permissions require a runtime route dump.

title: Identify roles and trust boundaries
assessment: Admin/content API strategies exist. Effective roles and object ownership policies require the deployed permission store and test accounts.

title: Lightweight threat model
assessment: A scoped top-ten threat model is included. Ranking is provisional without deployment and business context.

title: Tech stack and dependency fingerprint
assessment: Strapi 5.57.0 monorepo; Node.js, TypeScript/JavaScript, React admin, Koa, Knex, optional GraphQL/Apollo, Yarn 4 workspaces and SQL/SQLite providers.

title: SQL / NoSQL injection
assessment: Query helper validates operators; controllers validate query input. Raw-query candidates are inventoried, not exhaustively taint-traced.

title: OS command injection
assessment: Shell/dynamic-code candidates include CLI/build paths. No confirmed HTTP-input-to-command exploit was established; full tracing remains.

title: Path traversal & file I/O
assessment: URL filenames use basename and upload paths use generated hash/ext. Archive extraction and symlink safety need a complete path review.

title: Unsafe deserialization
assessment: JavaScript source and dependency manifests were inspected. No blanket assurance for all serializers or installed extensions is justified.

title: DOM-based & server-side XSS
assessment: WYSIWYG preview sanitizes output with DOMPurify. This is a positive control, not proof that every rendering context is safe.

title: Server-side request forgery (code level)
assessment: URL import checks DNS once then fetch follows redirects; DNS lookup is not pinned to the connection. F04 partially mitigated; webhook egress also needs review.

title: Server-side template injection (SSTI)
assessment: Email templating is used. Administrator-authored template reachability and safe interpolation need a complete review.

title: XXE and XML handling
assessment: SVG/XML-like uploads are accepted under allowlists. No complete parser configuration inventory or XXE execution test was performed.

title: LDAP / XPath / header / log injection
assessment: Webhook headers and public errors carry configured values. LDAP/XPath applicability and CRLF/log encoding paths are not fully established.

title: Open redirects and unvalidated forwards
assessment: OAuth callback validation compares exact origin and pathname. Other redirect paths and query-parameter abuse require review.

title: Prototype pollution & unsafe object merging (JS)
assessment: Object merging is present; OSV flags a GraphQL utility dependency. Untrusted-data reachability is not confirmed.

title: Regular-expression DoS (ReDoS)
assessment: Regular expressions were inventoried selectively. No recheck/RE2 or adversarial timing analysis across all regexes was completed.

title: File upload handling (code)
assessment: Default local upload storage is under the public directory, not a separate origin. SVG allowance depends on config. F12 remains; no XSS exploit is asserted.

title: Insecure use of reflection, dynamic code, and eval
assessment: Dynamic-code candidates are locations for follow-up, not demonstrated input-to-eval paths.

title: BOLA / IDOR
assessment: ID-based lookups are present. Router authorization does not prove object ownership; intended access policy and cross-user tests are missing.

title: Multi-tenant isolation
assessment: No target tenant model or tenant contract was supplied. Do not assume generic framework queries implement application tenant isolation.

title: Mass assignment / request binding
assessment: Core CRUD sanitizes input, but user update spreads request body. Role and sensitive-field restrictions require route/permission validation before declaring an exploit.

title: Function-level access control (BFLA)
assessment: Central authenticate/verify middleware exists, with explicit auth:false support. Every route and granted permission must be checked.

title: Property-level authorization (excessive data exposure)
assessment: Output sanitization and private password/token fields are observed. Per-role serializer coverage is not complete.

title: Privilege escalation paths
assessment: User creation/update supports roles. Effective route permissions and elevated-actor checks must be tested; no privilege escalation is asserted.

title: Authorization tests exist
assessment: Repository tests exist, but no proof of an exhaustive role-by-endpoint and cross-tenant test matrix was obtained.

title: Password and credential handling
assessment: Known example SQL passwords and signing/encryption fallback values exist. F02 is source-remediated in listed configs; rotation and TLS remain operator tasks.

title: Account recovery and verification flows
assessment: Reset tokens had no stored expiry. F05 adds expiry and rejects legacy links, but atomic one-time consumption and confirmation expiry remain unresolved.

title: Session management
assessment: Legacy mode uses long-lived stateless JWTs and has no logout endpoint. Refresh mode also swallowed revocation errors. F08/F09 need session migration and runtime replay tests.

title: JWT implementation
assessment: Algorithm is pinned, but legacy verification supplies no issuer/audience constraints and defaults to 30-day tokens. F09 remains; application claim policy is needed.

title: MFA implementation
assessment: No deployed MFA policy, enrollment or recovery configuration was supplied. Absence of a demonstrated MFA bypass is not a pass.

title: OAuth / OIDC / SSO
assessment: Callback URL checks exist. Provider state, nonce, PKCE and verified-email linking require provider-specific configuration and tests.

title: CSRF defenses
assessment: Refresh cookies use SameSite defaults; the patch enables Apollo CSRF prevention. Cookie-based write and refresh endpoints still need cross-site testing.

title: Race conditions (TOCTOU)
assessment: Reset-token read and password update remain separate operations. Two parallel requests may consume the same link. F05 remains partially fixed pending atomic consumption.

title: Workflow step bypasses
assessment: Confirmation/block state is checked during local login. No full onboarding/approval state-machine audit was completed.

title: Numeric edge cases and financial logic
assessment: No identified deployed financial workflow. App/plugin business requirements are needed before calling this not applicable.

title: Replay and idempotency
assessment: One-time token updates are non-atomic and outgoing webhooks lack receiver dedup context. Payment/inbound-event applicability is unknown.

title: Abuse of legitimate features
assessment: Auth rate-limit hooks exist. Search/export/invitation quotas and distributed behavior are not proven.

title: Time-based logic
assessment: Lifespans are server-configured. Patch adds server-time reset expiry; DST/boundary/session clock tests are still required.

title: Hardcoded credentials and secrets
assessment: Fallback credentials exist. F02 removes those in listed configs. Pattern inventory omits secret values; git history was excluded and no full Gitleaks history scan occurred.

title: Password hashing
assessment: bcrypt hashing defaults to cost 10; verification uses bcrypt.compare. Configurable costs, legacy hashes and password-length policy require validation.

title: Symmetric encryption
assessment: Export encryption defaults to AES-128-ECB with fixed empty KDF salt; CBC options derive IV from the key. F06 remains; changing format requires coordinated import/export migration.

title: Randomness
assessment: Reset tokens and GCM IVs use crypto.randomBytes. Other random values were not comprehensively classified by security purpose.

title: Signature and MAC verification
assessment: An audit-log export token uses constant-time comparison; JWT library performs verification. Every signature path has not been verified.

title: TLS usage in outbound calls
assessment: Fetch relies on platform TLS checks. Custom proxy/provider trust stores and environment-level overrides need deployment review.

title: Key management
assessment: Admin encryption key is configured via environment; fallback removed. No KMS, cross-environment isolation or rotation plan was supplied.

title: Fail-closed behavior
assessment: Logout swallowed revoke exceptions and returned success. F08 now returns an error on exceptions; non-throwing failures and other fallback paths need review.

title: Sensitive data in logs
assessment: URL-containing errors and fetch debug messages can expose user-influenced values. Central redaction and log-retention behavior need review.

title: Security event logging
assessment: Audit-log capability and denial responses exist. Actual enabled logging, SIEM forwarding, alerts and request IDs are not verified.

title: Debug and default configuration
assessment: Examples enable verbose logs/MCP and carry weak secrets; helper server bound broadly. F01/F02 harden bindings/secrets, but example debug features remain review-required.

title: Input validation strategy
assessment: Boundary validation exists in core CRUD. Duplicate-key behavior, every custom route and body-size settings need verification.

title: Known-vulnerable dependencies
assessment: OSV queried all 2,838 root lockfile package/version pairs; 44 pairs matched 111 unique advisory IDs. F10 is advisory evidence, not proof of deployed reachability.

title: Lockfiles, pinned versions, and integrity hashes
assessment: Yarn lock has integrity checks, but Compose PostgreSQL tag was unpinned and MySQL only major-pinned. Patch requires operator-selected tested images/digests; other lockfiles not SCA-scanned.

title: Dangerous install scripts and unmaintained packages
assessment: Root postinstall runs husky. Install hooks were inventoried, not executed. Transitive install scripts and package maintenance require deeper review.

title: CORS policy
assessment: Baseline wildcard origin reflects request Origin with credentials enabled. F03 denies cross-origin by default; no running-browser verification was performed.

title: TLS and HSTS
assessment: HSTS middleware exists. No TLS endpoint, certificate chain, reverse proxy or HTTPS redirect was supplied.

title: HTTP security headers
assessment: Documentation/playground paths add unsafe-inline and broad script exceptions. F11 remains; nonce-compatible UI migration and deployed header checks are required.

title: Cookie attributes
assessment: HttpOnly/SameSite cookie options exist; Secure depends on environment/proxy and overrides. All auth cookies were not checked on the wire.

title: Caching of sensitive responses
assessment: No deployed cache/proxy behavior was available. Sensitive responses must be tested for Cache-Control:no-store.

title: Subdomain and DNS hygiene
evidence: No DNS/host inventory supplied; no source file/line can establish deployed DNS hygiene.
assessment: Subdomain ownership, dangling CNAMEs and staging exposure require the approved host list.
evidence_full: No DNS/host inventory supplied; no source file/line can establish deployed DNS hygiene.

title: Content security reporting
assessment: No collected CSP-reporting infrastructure was supplied. Test reporting destinations and owners in deployment.

title: JWT runtime tests
assessment: Static verification constrains algorithms. No token-tampering, foreign-audience or signature tests against a running app were conducted.

title: Session revocation
assessment: Focused mocked logout error test passes after patch. Actual old access/refresh token replay after logout/password/role changes remains untested.

title: Rate limiting and anti-automation
assessment: Auth rate-limit hooks exist. No distributed-store, forwarded-IP spoofing or concurrent limit checks against a deployed service.

title: Error suppression
assessment: Generic internal-error formatting is observed. Malformed-body and exception tests on all public surfaces were not run.

title: Authorization runtime verification (BOLA/BFLA)
assessment: No two-user/two-tenant/admin test accounts or running app supplied. BOLA/BFLA runtime verification remains mandatory.

title: User enumeration
assessment: Login errors are generic for absent/wrong credentials, but blocked/unconfirmed responses differ. Enumeration timing and registration behavior remain untested.

title: Password policy and MFA enforcement
assessment: Model minimum password length is six; deployment validation/MFA policy unknown. No live weak/breached-password tests were performed.

title: Session handling in practice
assessment: Configured session lifespans are visible. Fixation, concurrent sessions, idle expiry and actual cookie scope are not runtime-tested.

title: CSRF runtime check
assessment: Browser cross-site JSON/multipart/refresh tests are deferred. SameSite or Apollo settings alone do not prove CSRF protection.

title: SSRF and cloud metadata access
assessment: Mocked tests cover blocked DNS answers and redirect:error. No cloud metadata/internal network/OOB probes were run; DNS-rebinding risk remains.

title: HTTP request smuggling and desync
evidence: No deployed proxy chain supplied; no source file/line proves parser agreement.
assessment: Request-smuggling tests need front/back proxy topology and separately approved safe runtime testing.
evidence_full: No deployed proxy chain supplied; no source file/line proves parser agreement.

title: Host header and routing attacks
assessment: Reset URLs use configured base URLs. Forwarded-header trust, host routing and virtual-host isolation need deployment validation.

title: Web cache poisoning and deception
evidence: No cache/CDN configuration supplied; source line evidence unavailable.
assessment: Unkeyed-header poisoning and path-confusion behavior require the actual cache configuration.
evidence_full: No cache/CDN configuration supplied; source line evidence unavailable.

title: Inbound webhook verification
assessment: Observed runner is outgoing, not proof of inbound webhook validation. Installed inbound payment/provider integrations are unknown.

title: WebSockets and server-sent events
assessment: GraphQL subscriptions default off. Other data-transfer/admin SSE/WebSocket authentication and origin checks need testing.

title: Exposed internal services
assessment: Source exposed development services. Bind patches reduce default exposure; no public port scan or cloud firewall inspection occurred.

title: Disable introspection and suggestions in production
assessment: Patch disables production introspection by default. Suggestion suppression and real enabled-plugin behavior remain unverified.

title: Query depth, complexity, and cost limits
assessment: Baseline maxLimit:-1 and unset depth only trigger warnings. F07 sets finite depth/pagination; cost/alias amplification limits still need implementation.

title: Batching and alias abuse
assessment: Patch explicitly disables HTTP batching. Alias-based amplification and per-operation rate accounting remain unresolved.

title: Field-level authorization
assessment: Top-level and configured-field authorization exist; unconfigured nested fields do not automatically inherit object ownership. Cross-role/tenant queries need tests.

title: Persisted queries and input validation
assessment: Typed schema generation exists. Persisted query allowlists and custom resolver input coverage were not supplied.

title: API gateway controls
evidence: S42:398-405; no gateway deployment configuration supplied
assessment: Loopback defaults narrow direct access. Gateway-only reachability, quotas and consistent API version policy need actual topology.
evidence_full: packages/core/core/src/Strapi.ts:398-405; no gateway deployment configuration supplied

title: Inventory and shadow APIs
assessment: Partial source route inventory is delivered. Enabled dynamic endpoints, JS bundles and version ownership require runtime inventory.

title: Reflected, stored, and DOM XSS runtime tests
assessment: Static WYSIWYG sanitizer verified. No reflected/stored/DOM browser payload tests were executed.

title: Clickjacking
assessment: Sameorigin frameguard is configured; sensitive pages must be tested against required frame-ancestors policy.

title: Sensitive data in client storage and bundles
assessment: Admin remember-me mode writes access JWTs to localStorage. F09 remains; no public bundle/source-map inspection was possible.

title: Third-party scripts
assessment: Documentation/playground permits third-party CDN scripts. Actual SRI, deployed script inventory and integrity policy are unverified.

title: postMessage and cross-origin communication
assessment: Preview postMessage locations are inventoried. Sender origin/receiver checks require targeted review and browser tests.

title: Upload abuse tests
assessment: MIME detection and extension exceptions exist. No active SVG, polyglot, decompression or oversized upload tests were performed.

title: Download and export features
assessment: Signed URL/token controls observed. Cross-user downloads, CSV formula injection and actual URL expiry remain untested.

title: Document and image processors
assessment: Native image/file processing dependencies exist; sandbox, network isolation and resource budgets are deployment-dependent and untested.

title: Public cloud storage and backups
assessment: No public storage enumeration or web-root backup probes were run. Public directory uploads are not proof of bucket misconfiguration.

title: Container and orchestrator exposure
assessment: Compose files were reviewed. Docker daemon/Kubernetes API/firewall exposure cannot be established from source.

title: Default pages, versions, and verbose banners
assessment: Development documentation/example features are present. Deployed default pages and version banners are unknown.

title: Denial-of-service resilience
assessment: No load/DoS testing was authorized for remote systems or performed. Finite GraphQL defaults mitigate only some resource risks.

title: Verify that attacks are detected
evidence: No SIEM/WAF access or detection logs supplied; source-line evidence unavailable.
assessment: Representative attacks must be correlated to alerts with owners/runbooks in staging.
evidence_full: No SIEM/WAF access or detection logs supplied; source-line evidence unavailable.

title: WAF and bot controls tuned
evidence: No WAF/bot configuration supplied; source-line evidence unavailable.
assessment: Blocking mode, false positives and independent application defenses require operational review.
evidence_full: No WAF/bot configuration supplied; source-line evidence unavailable.

title: Rate findings consistently
assessment: Qualitative severity/rationale and proposed owning teams are included. Production business context and confirmed reachability are missing, so final CVSS scores are not assigned.

title: Provide reproducible evidence and fixes
assessment: Each finding includes baseline file/line, code evidence, impact, fix or explicit open remediation, and verification scope.

title: Fix root causes, not instances
assessment: Repeated binding/secret defaults are patched across generators/configs. Architectural auth, SSRF, crypto and token-storage fixes remain open.

title: Retest
assessment: Nineteen focused mocked/source-level test groups pass and patch applicability is verified. Full build/typecheck and runtime retest remain undone.

title: Feed results back into the SDLC
assessment: Regression harness and follow-up plan delivered. CI integration, policy tests and custom Semgrep/CodeQL rules remain operator work.

title: Track trends
assessment: A baseline exists. Historical remediation time, recurrence and full endpoint coverage metrics were not supplied.
